mainTopic: Partial חליצה and spitting, heavenly decrees and how they can be undone, and spitting blood in חליצה
overview: The גמרא finishes a ברייתא about a יבמה who did only part of חליצה, and proves it follows רבי עקיבא. According to רבי עקיבא, spitting alone makes her forbidden to the brothers. The reason is that spitting comes at the end of חליצה, so people might think a full חליצה happened. A story with רבי אמי then teaches that if she spat before removing the shoe, she just removes it and does not spit again, because the order is not essential. Next, לוי is asked three questions: whether an armless woman can do חליצה, whether spitting blood counts, and what 'writing of truth' in דניאל means. This leads to a discussion of heavenly decrees: one sealed with a שבועה, like the one on בית עלי, cannot be undone by קרבנות, but תורה and גמילות חסדים can still help. A decree on a צבור can be torn up through prayer at any time, while a יחיד has the ten days between ראש השנה and יום הכפורים. The גמרא then returns to a יבמה who spat blood and explains when blood comes with saliva. Finally, it quotes the next line of the משנה about a חרש and חליצה.

steps.title: The ברייתא's three cases of incomplete חליצה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives three rulings. If she removed the shoe without spitting or reciting, the חליצה is valid. If she only spat, the חליצה is flawed. If she only recited, nothing happened at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: [If she removed the shoe but did not] spit and did not recite, her חליצה is valid. If she spat but did not remove the shoe and did not recite, her חליצה is flawed. If she recited but did not spit and did not remove the shoe, there is nothing here to worry about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from a ברייתא that lists what happens when a יבמה does only one part of חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three parts to חליצה: removing the shoe, spitting, and reciting the פסוקים. Removing the shoe alone is enough. Spitting alone does something, but it is flawed. Reciting alone does nothing at all.

keyTerms.meaning: She removed the shoe from the יבם's foot
She spat in front of the יבם
She recited the פסוקים of חליצה
Flawed; it has some effect but is not a proper חליצה
Grounds for concern; here, nothing to worry about

phrases.english: [If she removed the shoe but did not] spit and did not recite —
her ḥalitza is valid.
If she spat but did not remove the shoe and did not recite —
her ḥalitza is flawed.
If she recited but did not spit and did not remove the shoe —
there is nothing here to be concerned about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted at the end of the previous daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Removing the shoe alone makes the חליצה valid. Spitting alone makes it flawed. Reciting alone has no effect.

steps.title: Whose view is the ברייתא? Maybe רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who wrote the ברייתא and tries out the idea that it is רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If you say it is רבי אליעזר, would he really say that if she removed the shoe without spitting or reciting, her חליצה is valid?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion the ברייתא follows. It suggests רבי אליעזר, already sounding doubtful, and is setting up a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's first ruling says removing the shoe alone is enough, so spitting is not needed. The גמרא checks whether this can fit רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (it is suggesting an option)

phrases.english: Whose view is this?
If you say it is Rabbi Eliezer:
if she removed the shoe but did not spit and did not recite,
is her ḥalitza valid?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks who wrote the ברייתא just quoted

steps.title: רבי אליעזר holds every action is essential
steps.stepSummary: It cannot be רבי אליעזר, because he learns from ככה יעשה that any part of חליצה that is an action, including spitting, is essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי אליעזר said: "So shall it be done" teaches that anything that is an action is essential!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רבי אליעזר as the author, because he requires spitting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, spitting is an action, so a חליצה without it should not work. The ברייתא says removing the shoe alone is valid, so it cannot be his view.

keyTerms.meaning: "So shall it be done" (the פסוק about חליצה)
An action, as opposed to speech
Essential; without it the act does not work

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Eliezer say:
"So shall it be done"
anything that is an action is essential!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion that the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבי אליעזר wrote the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר requires every action, including spitting, but the ברייתא says a חליצה without spitting is valid.

steps.title: So the ברייתא must be רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: Since it cannot be רבי אליעזר, the ברייתא clearly follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obviously רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא is רבי עקיבא's view. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that only an action done on the יבם's body, removing the shoe, is essential. That fits the ruling that removing the shoe alone is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; switching to a different answer

phrases.english: Rather, it is obviously Rabbi Akiva,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the remaining option after רבי אליעזר was ruled out

steps.title: Flawed to whom?
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא's ברייתא says that if she only spat, the חליצה is flawed. The גמרא asks: forbidden to whom?
steps.simpleTranslation: And it teaches: if she spat but did not remove the shoe and did not recite, her חליצה is flawed. To whom is she forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא focuses on the middle ruling of the ברייתא and asks what "flawed" means. It is setting up a proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A flawed חליצה could mean one of two things. She might now be forbidden to the brothers, or she might still be forbidden to everyone else. The גמרא wants to know which.

keyTerms.meaning: A flawed חליצה; it does not fully free her

phrases.english: And it teaches: if she spat but did not remove the shoe
and did not recite, her ḥalitza is flawed.
To whom?
phrases.notes: He means: to whom is she now forbidden to marry because of this?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָתָנֵי: רָקְקָה וְלֹא חָלְצָה וְלֹא קָרְאָה — חֲלִיצָתָהּ פְּסוּלָה. לְמַאן?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the ברייתא is רבי עקיבא's, it looks closely at its middle ruling
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the flawed חליצה forbids her to the brothers or to everyone else

steps.title: It cannot mean forbidden to everyone
steps.stepSummary: Saying she is still forbidden to the world would be obvious, since no real חליצה took place to free her.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say she is forbidden to the world, that is obvious! Was there any חליצה that would make her permitted to the world?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the reading that "flawed" means she stays forbidden to other men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She never removed the shoe, so of course she is not free to marry anyone else. A ברייתא would not bother teaching something that obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: To the world; to any other man
Was there at all? (a rhetorical question)

phrases.english: If you say to the world, that is obvious!
Was there any ḥalitza at all
that she should be permitted to the world?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules out the first possible answer to "to whom"
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that "flawed" means forbidden to the world
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would be too obvious to teach, since no real חליצה happened.

steps.title: Spitting alone forbids her to the brothers
steps.stepSummary: So "flawed" must mean she is now forbidden to the brothers. This proves that according to רבי עקיבא, spitting alone has that effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not to the brothers? Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that, according to רבי עקיבא, spitting alone forbids the יבמה to the brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spitting is not essential for a valid חליצה according to רבי עקיבא. Even so, it does something real: she can no longer do יבום with any of the brothers.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not? (leading to a proof)
To the brothers of the dead husband
Learn from this; it is proven

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי עקיבא, removing the shoe alone is a valid חליצה. Spitting alone forbids her to the brothers but does not free her to marry others. Reciting alone does nothing.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not to the brothers?
Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the only remaining answer to "to whom" and treats it as proven
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי עקיבא, spitting alone forbids the יבמה to the brothers.

steps.title: Why is spitting different from reciting?
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי עקיבא, neither spitting nor reciting is essential. So why does spitting forbid her to the brothers while reciting does nothing?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי עקיבא, what is different about spitting, and what is different about reciting?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new difficulty. It asks why רבי עקיבא treats spitting and reciting differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, only removing the shoe is essential, so spitting and reciting seem to have the same status. Yet the ברייתא says spitting alone forbids her to the brothers, while reciting alone means nothing. The גמרא wants a reason for the difference.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Akiva,
what is different about spitting,
and what is different about reciting?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, מַאי שְׁנָא רְקִיקָה וּמַאי שְׁנָא קְרִיָּיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that spitting forbids her to the brothers and asks why reciting does not
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's different treatment of spitting and reciting according to רבי עקיבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both are non-essential according to רבי עקיבא, yet only spitting forbids her to the brothers.

steps.title: Spitting can be mistaken for a finished חליצה, but reciting cannot
steps.stepSummary: Reciting happens both before and after the shoe removal, so nobody will be misled by it. Spitting only happens at the end, so people might think a full חליצה took place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reciting happens at the beginning and at the end, so people will not get confused. Spitting only happens at the end, so people will get confused and come to permit a real חלוצה to the brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 8: why does spitting forbid her to the brothers while reciting does not?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is a protective גזירה, not a claim that spitting is part of the core act. Someone who sees her recite knows it may be only the opening words. Someone who sees her spit assumes the shoe was already removed, so if she were allowed to the brothers, people would think a real חלוצה is allowed to them too.

keyTerms.meaning: The reciting of the פסוקים during חליצה
Spitting, done by the יבמה during חליצה
It gets mixed up or mistaken for something else
A woman who has already done a valid חליצה

steps.confusionAlert: Spitting alone is not a valid חליצה. She is forbidden to the brothers only as a safeguard, so people do not confuse her with a real חלוצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This idea, that spitting looks like the end of חליצה, drives the rest of the sugya, including the story with רבי אמי.

phrases.aramaic: קְרִיָּיה, דְּאִיתַהּ בֵּין בַּתְּחִלָּה בֵּין בַּסּוֹף —
phrases.english: The recitation, which is there both at the beginning and at the end
will not be mistaken by him.
Spitting, which is not at the beginning but is at the end
will be mistaken by him,
and they will come to permit a woman who did חליצה to the brothers.

steps.triggerLanguage: קְרִיָּיה, דְּאִיתַהּ בֵּין בַּתְּחִלָּה בֵּין בַּסּוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical distinction: risk of mistaken appearance
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Spitting and reciting are equal for רבי עקיבא, since neither is essential
steps.terutzMaskana: Spitting looks like the end of חליצה, so the חכמים forbade her to the brothers. Reciting does not look like that.

steps.title: Another version: a יבמה who spat first just removes the shoe
steps.stepSummary: Another version of the message that was sent says a יבמה who spat before the removal does the removal and does not spit again.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say this is the message they sent: a יבמה who spat should do חליצה, and she does not need to spit another time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the ruling that was sent: if she spat first, she just removes the shoe and does not spit again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the earlier spit counts. Asking her to spit again might suggest the first spit meant nothing. The next step brings a story that shows this ruling in action.

phrases.english: And there are those who say
this is what they sent to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is the person the message was sent to earlier in the sugya, the father of שמואל.

phrases.english: A יבמה who spat should remove the shoe,
and she does not need to spit another time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version of the message sent to the father of שמואל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If she spat before the removal, she removes the shoe and does not spit again.

steps.title: The story before רבי אמי
steps.stepSummary: A woman spat before removing the shoe. רבי אמי ruled that she should just remove it, and then her case is closed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the woman who came before רבי אמי while רבי אבא בר ממל was sitting there. She spat before doing the removal. רבי אמי said: have her remove the shoe and close her case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real case that matches the ruling in step 10. It is also setting up the back-and-forth between רבי אבא and רבי אמי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי does not ask for a second spitting. He has her finish with the removal and lets her go. This matches the ruling that one spit is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarrel or dispute, here meaning her case in court

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הַהִיא דַּאֲתַאי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי,
phrases.english: Like that woman who came before Rabbi Ami,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה יָתֵיב רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל קַמֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Abba bar Memel was sitting before him.
She spat before she removed the shoe.
Rabbi Ami said to him:
Have her remove the shoe, and close her dispute.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הַהִיא דַּאֲתַאי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the ruling of step 10 in a real case
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that she does not spit again
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case decided by רבי אמי

steps.title: But חליצה needs spitting
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא objects that חליצה requires spitting, and none came after the removal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to him: but we need spitting!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא challenges רבי אמי: how can she finish without spitting?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah lists spitting as part of the חליצה ceremony. רבי אבא assumes that if the removal comes now, a spit must follow it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to him:
But we need spitting!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אמי's ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's ruling to skip another spit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Spitting is part of the ceremony, so it cannot just be left out.

steps.title: She already spat
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי answers that the spitting was already done.
steps.simpleTranslation: She already spat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי answers that the spitting requirement is already fulfilled by her earlier spit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He treats the earlier spit as counting, even though it came before the removal.

phrases.english: She already spat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אבא's challenge
steps.terutzMaskana: The earlier spit counts as the required spitting.

steps.title: Why not just have her spit again?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא asks what harm there would be in having her spit a second time.
steps.simpleTranslation: So let her spit again. What is wrong with that?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא pushes back: even if the first spit counts, a second one costs nothing, so why not do it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is suggesting a safer route that clearly follows the proper order. The challenge forces רבי אמי to explain why a second spit would actually cause harm.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is wrong with that?

phrases.english: So let her spit, and what is wrong with that?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The refusal to have her spit again
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second spit seems harmless and would satisfy everyone.

steps.title: A second spit would teach people that spitting means nothing
steps.stepSummary: If she spits again, people will think the first spit had no meaning. They will then come to permit a real חלוצה to the brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: A disaster would come from it. If you say she should spit again, people will say the first spitting has no substance, and they will come to permit a חלוצה to the brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי explains that a second spit would cause real damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the same worry as step 9. People who see spitting assume the shoe was already removed. If we act as though that spit meant nothing, they will conclude that a woman who spat, and so seemed to have finished חליצה, is still allowed to the brothers.

keyTerms.meaning: She should go back and do it again

steps.whatToRemember: A spit is never treated as meaningless, because that could lead people to permit a real חלוצה to the brothers.

phrases.english: A disaster would come out of it,
because if you say she should go back and spit,

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי: רְקִיקָה קַמַּיְיתָא לֵית בַּהּ מְשָׁשָׁא,
phrases.english: people will say: the first spitting has no substance,
and they will come to permit a woman who did חליצה to the brothers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the harm in the suggested alternative
steps.terutzMaskana: A second spit would make people treat spitting as meaningless, which leads to a serious mistake.

steps.title: But the acts must be done in order
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא objects that the removal and the spitting must follow the order the Torah lists.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we need them done in their order!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא raises a new objection: here the spit came before the removal, which is the wrong order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah describes removing the shoe first and then spitting. If order matters, a spit done first should not count.

phrases.english: But we need them in their order!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New challenge to the claim that the early spit counts
steps.kashyaTarget: Counting a spit that came before the removal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the order is required, an early spit is not valid.

steps.title: The order is not essential
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי answers that doing them in order is not essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doing them in order does not hold it back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי answers that the order is preferred, but getting it wrong does not ruin the חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Not essential" means that after the fact it still works. So the early spit still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Does not hold it back, is not essential after the fact

phrases.english: Their order is not essential.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying that a detail is not essential
steps.terutzMaskana: Doing the acts out of order is still valid after the fact.

steps.title: A ברייתא proves רבי אמי was right
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא thought he was being brushed off. Later he checked and found a ברייתא saying the order does not matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא thought: he is just pushing me off. He went out, checked, and found that it is taught: whether the removal came before the spitting or the spitting came before the removal, what was done is done.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with a ברייתא that proves רבי אמי's answer was correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא first suspected the answers were made up to dodge his questions. The ברייתא shows that a real source says either order is valid, so the early spit counts.

keyTerms.meaning: He is just pushing him off with weak answers
What he did is done, it is valid

steps.whatToRemember: A spit done before the removal of the shoe still counts. She removes the shoe and does not spit again.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא סָבַר: דַּחוֹיֵי קָא מְדַחֵי לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: He thought: he is just pushing him off.
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי אבא, who felt רבי אמי was dodging his questions.

phrases.english: He went out, examined, and found,
as it is taught in a ברייתא:
Whether the removal was done before the spitting,
or the spitting was done before the removal,
what he did is done.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 17 with a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: That the order of removal and spitting is not essential
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: either order, what was done is done
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Spitting before the removal is valid, so no second spit is needed.

steps.title: לוי is asked three questions in the villages
steps.stepSummary: לוי goes out to the villages. People ask him whether an armless woman can do חליצה, whether spitting blood counts, and what the 'writing of truth' in דניאל implies.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי went out to the villages. They asked him: An armless woman, may she do חליצה? A יבמה who spat blood, what is the law? And the פסוק says 'But I will tell you what is written in the writing of truth.' Does that mean there is writing that is not true?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story in which people ask לוי three questions. This sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two questions test whether חליצה needs hands and real saliva, since the Torah says 'remove the shoe' and 'spit.' The third question is about how to read a פסוק. If one heavenly writing is called 'true,' it sounds like some other writing is not true.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman without hands or arms
By implication; from this we would learn

phrases.english: Levi went out to the villages.
They asked him:
An armless woman, may she perform חליצה?
A yevama who spat blood, what is the law?
"But I will tell you
that which is inscribed in the writing of truth"
By implication, there is
writing that is not true?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After learning that the order of חליצה is not essential, the גמרא brings another story about how strictly to follow the Torah's wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can חליצה be done without hands? Is spitting blood valid? Does 'writing of truth' imply that some heavenly writing is untrue?

steps.title: The בית מדרש answers the two חליצה questions
steps.stepSummary: לוי did not know the answers, so he asked in the בית מדרש. They answered that the פסוק does not say 'by hand' and does not say 'saliva.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He did not have an answer. He came and asked in the בית מדרש, and they told him: Does it say 'and she shall remove the shoe by hand'? And does it say 'and she shall spit saliva'?
steps.whatsHappening: The בית מדרש answers the two חליצה questions. Both are valid: an armless woman may do חליצה, and spitting blood counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says only 'she shall remove' and 'she shall spit,' with no mention of hands or saliva. So we may not add conditions the Torah did not write. Removing the shoe any way works, and spitting anything works.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not have it in hand; he did not know the answer

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common method: when a פסוק leaves a detail out, we do not make that detail a requirement.

phrases.english: He did not have it in hand.
phrases.notes: He means he didn't know the answer.

phrases.english: He came and asked in the study hall.
They said to him:
Is it written "and she shall remove it by hand"?
And is it written "and she shall spit saliva"?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא הֲוָה בִּידֵיהּ. אֲתָא שַׁאֵיל בֵּי מִדְרְשָׁא, אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first two questions from step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An armless woman may do חליצה, and spitting blood is valid, because the פסוק requires neither hands nor saliva.

steps.title: The writing of truth question is raised again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats the third question: if the פסוק speaks of 'writing of truth,' is there heavenly writing that is not true?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'But I will tell you what is inscribed in the writing of truth.' But is there any writing that is not true?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the third question so it can answer it. This step sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling one writing 'true' seems to imply that other heavenly writing is false. That is impossible, so the wording of the פסוק needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: That which is inscribed or recorded

phrases.english: "But I will tell you
that which is inscribed in the writing of truth"
But is there writing that is not true?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the third question from step 19, which step 20 left unanswered.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'writing of truth' in דניאל 10:21
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one writing is called 'true,' it implies some heavenly writing is untrue, which cannot be.

steps.title: A decree sealed with an oath versus one without
steps.stepSummary: The 'writing of truth' is a heavenly גזר דין sealed with a שבועה. A גזר דין without a שבועה is not called 'true' in this sense, because it can still change.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here it means a decree that comes with an oath. There it means a decree that does not come with an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the third question. Heavenly decrees come in two kinds: those sealed with a שבועה and those without.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'True' here means final and permanent, not 'as opposed to false.' A גזר דין with a שבועה can never be canceled. One without a שבועה can still be changed, so it is not called 'writing of truth.'

keyTerms.meaning: A decree; a sentence of judgment

steps.whatToRemember: All three questions are answered by reading the פסוק carefully. No hands or saliva are required for חליצה. 'Writing of truth' means a heavenly decree sealed with a שבועה, which cannot be canceled.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Not true' does not mean false. It means a decree that can still be changed.

phrases.english: It is not difficult.

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן בִּגְזַר דִּין שֶׁיֵּשׁ עִמּוֹ שְׁבוּעָה.
phrases.english: Here, it is a decree that comes with an oath.
phrases.notes: This is the 'writing of truth.' Sealed with an oath, it can never be undone.

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן בִּגְזַר דִּין שֶׁאֵין עִמּוֹ שְׁבוּעָה.
phrases.english: There, it is a decree that does not come with an oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בִּגְזַר דִּין שֶׁיֵּשׁ עִמּוֹ שְׁבוּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between two kinds of heavenly decrees
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Writing of truth' implies some heavenly writing is false.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Writing of truth' means a decree sealed with an oath, which cannot be canceled. Other decrees can still change.

steps.title: The source: an oath against בית עלי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן proves from the oath against בית עלי that a גזר דין made with a שבועה cannot be torn up.
steps.simpleTranslation: This fits what רב שמואל בר אמי said in the name of רבי יונתן: How do we know that a sentence made with an oath cannot be torn up? Because the פסוק says, 'Therefore I have sworn to בית עלי that the sin of בית עלי will not be atoned with sacrifice or offering forever.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source for what it just said in step 22: a heavenly sentence that comes with an oath cannot change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 claimed that a גזר דין with a שבועה is the 'writing of truth' that stays fixed. Here רבי יונתן shows it from a פסוק: ה' swore about בית עלי, and the פסוק says their sin will never be atoned with קרבנות. The oath is what makes the sentence permanent.

keyTerms.meaning: A sentence or decree of judgment
The family of עלי the כהן

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole section: the sentence on בית עלי is the classic example of a sealed decree, and the next steps ask whether anything can still help.

phrases.english: This is in line with Rav Shmuel bar Ami.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַמֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן:
phrases.english: For Rav Shmuel bar Ami said that Rabbi Yonatan said:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לִגְזַר דִּין שֶׁיֵּשׁ עִמּוֹ שְׁבוּעָה
phrases.english: From where do we know that a sentence of judgment that comes with an oath
cannot be torn up?
As it says: "Therefore I have sworn to the house of Eli
that the sin of Eli's house will not be atoned for
with sacrifice or with offering, forever."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 3:14. In an oath, the word אִם means 'will not.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק source for the idea in step 22 that a גזר דין with a שבועה cannot change.
steps.raayaObject: A heavenly גזר דין that comes with a שבועה cannot be torn up.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א 3:14, the oath against בית עלי that their sin will never be atoned with קרבנות.

steps.title: Torah and kindness can still bring atonement
steps.stepSummary: רבה says בית עלי can find atonement through תורה; אביי says through גמילות חסדים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: With sacrifice and offering it is not atoned, but it is atoned through words of Torah. אביי said: With sacrifice and offering it is not atoned, but it is atoned through acts of kindness.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה and אביי read the same פסוק closely and point out that it only rules out קרבנות. They say other things can still bring atonement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names only 'זבח and מנחה.' So רבה learns that תורה learning can still atone, and אביי learns that גמילות חסדים can. The oath still stands, but it only blocks one road to atonement.
steps.confusionAlert: רבה and אביי are not saying the oath can be torn up. They are saying the oath only spoke about קרבנות, so other ways of atonement were never blocked.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה: בְּזֶבַח וּבְמִנְחָה אֵינוֹ מִתְכַּפֵּר,
phrases.english: Rabba said: With sacrifice and offering it is not atoned for,
but it is atoned for through words of Torah.

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: בְּזֶבַח וּבְמִנְחָה אֵינוֹ מִתְכַּפֵּר,
phrases.english: Abaye said: With sacrifice and offering it is not atoned for,
but it is atoned for through acts of kindness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: בְּזֶבַח וּבְמִנְחָה אֵינוֹ מִתְכַּפֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the פסוק from step 23 and shows its limits: only קרבנות are ruled out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The oath on בית עלי blocks atonement through קרבנות only. תורה (רבה) or גמילות חסדים (אביי) can still bring atonement.

steps.title: רבה and אביי's own lives
steps.stepSummary: רבה and אביי came from בית עלי. רבה, who learned תורה, lived 40 years; אביי, who learned and did kindness, lived 60.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and אביי came from בית עלי. רבה, who was busy with Torah, lived forty years. אביי, who was busy with Torah and acts of kindness, lived sixty years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us that רבה and אביי were themselves from בית עלי, and their lives show their own teachings in action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Members of בית עלי were cursed to die young. רבה lived longer through תורה, and אביי lived even longer because he added גמילות חסדים. This backs up the idea that these things help even against a sealed decree.

keyTerms.meaning: Was busy with, put effort into

phrases.english: Rabba and Abaye came from the house of Eli.
Rabba, who was busy with Torah,
lived forty years.
Abaye, who was busy with Torah and acts of kindness,
lived sixty years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the teachings of step 24 playing out in the lives of the very people who said them.
steps.raayaObject: תורה and גמילות חסדים help members of בית עלי despite the decree.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה lived 40 years with תורה; אביי lived 60 years with תורה and גמילות חסדים.

steps.title: The family that died at eighteen
steps.stepSummary: A family in ירושלים kept dying young. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי told them to learn תורה, and they lived.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: There was a family in ירושלים whose members died at about eighteen. They came and told רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. He said: Perhaps you are from the family of עלי, since the פסוק says, 'All the increase of your house will die as men.' Go and busy yourselves with Torah, and you will live. They went, learned Torah, and lived, and people called them 'the family of יוחנן,' after him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with another story showing that learning תורה saved members of בית עלי from dying young.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The curse said the men of בית עלי would die once they became adults. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי recognized the pattern and prescribed תורה learning. It worked, which supports רבה's view that תורה brings atonement where קרבנות cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: The increase of your house, your descendants

steps.whatToRemember: Even a decree sealed with a שבועה, like the one on בית עלי, can be softened through תורה and גמילות חסדים, though not through קרבנות.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
There was one family in Jerusalem

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיוּ מֵתִים כְּבֶן שְׁמֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה.
phrases.english: whose members would die at about eighteen years old.

phrases.aramaic: בָּאוּ וְהוֹדִיעוּ אֶת רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי.
phrases.english: They came and told Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: שֶׁמָּא מִמִּשְׁפַּחַת עֵלִי אַתֶּם,
phrases.english: He said to them: Perhaps you are from the family of Eli,
as it says: "And all the increase of your house will die as men."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 2:33. 'As men' means they die as soon as they grow into young adults.

phrases.english: Go and busy yourselves with Torah, and you will live.
They went and busied themselves with Torah, and they lived.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיוּ קוֹרִין אוֹתָן ״מִשְׁפַּחַת יוֹחָנָן״ עַל שְׁמוֹ.
phrases.english: And people would call them "the family of Yochanan," after his name.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִשְׁפָּחָה אַחַת הָיְתָה בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second story, from a ברייתא, supporting the idea that תורה saves members of בית עלי.
steps.raayaObject: תורה learning can save members of בית עלי from the decree of dying young.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a family in ירושלים saved by following רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's advice to learn תורה.

steps.title: A sentence on a community is never sealed
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that a גזר דין on a צבור is never sealed, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר אוניא said in the name of רב: From where do we know that a sentence on a community is never sealed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching on the same theme of fixed decrees: a decree against a whole community is never made final. It is setting up a search for a source, but the גמרא interrupts before the source is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we spoke about a decree on one family. רב now says that a decree on a צבור is different: it is never sealed, so the community can always change it. The source is about to be asked about, but the next step challenges the idea first.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אוּנְיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Unya said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לִגְזַר דִּין שֶׁל צִבּוּר שֶׁאֵינוֹ נֶחְתָּם?
phrases.english: From where do we know that a sentence of judgment on a community is not sealed?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אוּנְיָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a decree on one family to a decree on a whole community.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A heavenly גזר דין on a צבור is never sealed.

steps.title: Challenge: a פסוק says the community's sin is sealed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב from a פסוק in ירמיהו that seems to say Israel's sin is sealed before ה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not sealed?! But it is written: 'For if you wash with niter and use much soap, your sin is stained before Me!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised at רב's teaching and challenges it with a פסוק that seems to show a community's sin can be sealed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ירמיהו, ה' speaks to all of Israel and says that no amount of washing will remove their sin. The גמרא reads נכתם as if it says the sin is 'sealed,' which would contradict רב's claim that a decree on a צבור is never sealed.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? (opens a challenge from a פסוק)

phrases.english: It is not sealed?!
But isn't it written: "For if you wash yourself with niter
and use much soap,
your sin is stained before Me!"
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 2:22. The גמרא hears נִכְתָּם as close to נֶחְתָּם, 'sealed.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the teaching of רב in step 27 before its source is even given.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's teaching that a גזר דין on a צבור is never sealed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In ירמיהו 2:22 ה' tells the whole nation that its sin is 'נכתם' (read as sealed) before Him, which suggests a community's sentence can be sealed.

steps.title: Rewording רב: even a sealed decree can be torn up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords רב's teaching. It is not that a צבור's decree is never sealed. Rather, even once sealed, it can be torn up, as the פסוק says ה' is close 'whenever we call upon Him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what רב meant: from where do we know that even if the decree is sealed, it can be torn up? As it says: 'Who is like ה' our God whenever we call upon Him?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from ירמיהו by changing how we read רב's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ירמיהו showed that a sin can be sealed, so רב cannot mean a צבור's decree is never sealed. The new version agrees it can be sealed, but says prayer can still rip it up. The proof is that ה' answers the community every time they call.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; the גמרא is changing the earlier version

phrases.english: Rather: from where do we know
that even if it was sealed, it is torn up?
As it says: 'Who is like ה' our God'
'whenever we call to Him.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from ירמיהו by rewording רב
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A decree on a צבור is never sealed at all
steps.terutzMaskana: A decree on a צבור can be sealed, but it can still be torn up through prayer

steps.title: A פסוק that says to seek ה' only when He can be found
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: another פסוק says 'Seek ה' while He may be found,' which suggests ה' is not always close.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'Seek ה' while He may be found!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק that seems to clash with the proof from step 29.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ה' answers 'whenever we call,' why would we need to seek Him only 'while He may be found'? The second פסוק suggests there are special times when He is close, and other times when He is less so.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written... (introduces a contradicting פסוק)

phrases.english: But it is written: 'Seek ה' while He may be found!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the פסוק used as proof in step 29
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from 'whenever we call upon Him'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק says ה' is always reachable; another says to seek Him only at the times He can be found

steps.title: One פסוק is about a person alone, the other about a community
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: 'Seek ה' while He may be found' is about a יחיד, while 'whenever we call' is about a צבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a problem: this one is about an individual, and that one is about a community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the clash between the two פסוקים by giving each one a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A צבור can reach ה' at any time, so their sealed decree can always be torn up. A יחיד has to look for the special times when ה' is close.
steps.whatToRemember: A צבור can always tear up a decree through prayer; a יחיד must use the special times when ה' is close.

phrases.english: It is not a problem:
this is about an individual, that is about a community.
phrases.notes: 'Seek while He may be found' is the individual; 'whenever we call' is the community.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּיָחִיד, הָא בְּצִיבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 30
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both פסוקים speak about the same people, so they contradict
steps.terutzMaskana: Each פסוק speaks about a different group

steps.title: When is ה' close to an individual?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: for a יחיד, when is the time that ה' 'may be found'?
steps.simpleTranslation: For an individual, when is that time?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a יחיד must seek ה' 'while He may be found,' there must be a specific time. The גמרא wants to know what that time is.

phrases.english: An individual, when?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the answer in step 31
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The time when ה' is close to an individual

steps.title: The ten days between ראש השנה and יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה answers: the time is the ten days between ראש השנה and יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: these are the ten days between ראש השנה and יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 32 by naming the special time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During these ten days a יחיד has the same kind of closeness to ה' that a צבור always has. This finishes the topic of tearing up a decree.
steps.whatToRemember: A צבור can tear up a decree any time; a יחיד has the ten days from ראש השנה to יום הכפורים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous source for why the days between ראש השנה and יום הכפורים are a special time for תשובה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabbah bar Avuha:
These are the ten days
that are between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 32
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ten days between ראש השנה and יום הכפורים

steps.title: A יבמה who spat blood may do חליצה
steps.stepSummary: The sages sent a ruling to the father of שמואל: a יבמה who spat blood does חליצה, since blood always comes with some saliva.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent to the father of שמואל: a יבמה who spat blood should do חליצה, because blood cannot come out without a little saliva.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the topic of prayer and goes back to an earlier question about חליצה, bringing a ruling about a יבמה who spat blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In חליצה the יבמה must spit in front of the יבם. The question is whether spitting blood counts. The ruling says it does, because there is always some saliva mixed in with the blood.

keyTerms.meaning: They sent to him (a ruling sent by letter)
A widow whose husband's brother must do יבום or חליצה
She may do חליצה (remove the shoe)

phrases.english: They sent to Shmuel's father:
A yevamah who spat blood may do chalitzah,
because it is impossible for blood
without a trace of saliva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the prayer topic and returns to the earlier discussion of חליצה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A יבמה who spat blood may do חליצה, because blood always has some saliva in it

steps.title: Challenge from the blood of a זב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges from a ברייתא: blood that comes from a זב's mouth or from where his urine comes out is טהור. This suggests blood can come out without saliva.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: You might think blood coming from his mouth or from his urinary opening is impure. So the פסוק says 'his discharge is impure,' meaning blood coming from his mouth or urinary opening is not impure but pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about a זב to attack the ruling in step 34.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב's saliva is טמא. If blood could never come without saliva, then blood from a זב's mouth should be טמא because of the saliva in it. Since the ברייתא says it is טהור, it seems blood can come out with no saliva, so the יבמה's spitting may not count.

keyTerms.meaning: The opening where urine comes out

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not mention saliva or חליצה at all. The challenge is implied: if all blood had saliva in it, this blood would be טמא.

phrases.english: They challenged:
You might think that blood that comes out
from his mouth or from his urinary opening is impure,
phrases.notes: 'His' means a זב, whose saliva and urine are impure.

phrases.english: so the verse says: 'His discharge is impure,'
and blood that comes out
from his mouth or urinary opening is not impure,

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: יָכוֹל יְהֵא דָּם הַיּוֹצֵא מִפִּיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning of the ruling in step 34
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that blood cannot come out without saliva
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If blood always carried saliva, a זב's blood would be טמא because of the saliva; the ברייתא says it is טהור, so blood can come out without saliva

steps.title: Sucked-up blood versus dripping blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. The ruling sent to שמואל's father is about a יבמה who sucks the blood up into her mouth, so saliva comes along. The ברייתא about the זב is about blood that drips out by itself, which can come without saliva.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here (the יבמה) is a woman who sucks the blood up. There (the זב) is blood that drips out on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 35. It shows that the two sources are talking about two different ways blood leaves the mouth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed blood never leaves the mouth without saliva. The answer limits that rule to blood that is sucked up and then spat, since sucking brings saliva with it. Blood that simply flows out of a wound can come out clean, which is why the זב's blood can be טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult, the opening words of an answer
A woman who sucks (the blood up into her mouth)
Dripping or flowing out by itself
Here... there: one source is about one case, the other about a different case

steps.whatToRemember: A יבמה who spits blood has done valid חליצה because she sucks the blood up and saliva comes with it. A זב's blood that just drips out may have no saliva, so it is טהור.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, it is about a woman who sucks [the blood up],
phrases.notes: "Here" means the ruling sent to שמואל's father about the יבמה who spat blood.

phrases.english: there, it is about [blood] that drips out by itself.
phrases.notes: "There" means the ברייתא about blood coming from the mouth of a זב.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בְּמוֹצֶצֶת, כָּאן בְּשׁוֹתֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 35 by splitting the cases
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case distinction (כאן... כאן): the two sources are about different ways blood comes out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Blood from the mouth sometimes comes without saliva, so the ruling about the יבמה seems wrong
steps.terutzMaskana: Sucked-up blood always has saliva, so the יבמה's חליצה is valid. Dripping blood may have none, so the זב's blood is טהור

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about a deaf-mute and חליצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: a חרש who underwent חליצה. This opens a new topic.
steps.simpleTranslation: [We learned in the משנה:] A deaf-mute who underwent חליצה, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line of the משנה. It is setting up the discussion about a חרש and חליצה that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full משנה says that if a deaf-mute man or woman does חליצה, or a grown woman does חליצה with a boy who is a minor, the חליצה is invalid. The word "and so on" tells us the גמרא is quoting only the opening words.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute, who in הלכה is not considered fully able to take on legal acts
Underwent חליצה, the ceremony that frees a יבמה from יבום
And so on: the rest of the quote is left out

phrases.english: A deaf-mute who underwent חליצה, and so on.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. The rest says that a חרש's חליצה, or a woman's חליצה with a minor, is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the blood-and-saliva discussion and starts a new section of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חליצה of a חרש (or with a minor) is invalid
